title: Financial Procedures
description: Understanding Nepal's government financial procedures, budget process, and fiscal management.

sections.title: Budget Cycle Overview
sections.content: The financial year process includes drafting, legislative approval, execution, and auditing. Coordination across federal, provincial, and local levels ensures resource alignment with development priorities.

sections.title: Revenue Sources and Allocation
sections.content: Revenue derives from taxes, fees, grants, and shared revenues. Intergovernmental fiscal transfers aim to reduce disparities and fund constitutionally mandated services.

sections.title: Public Financial Management (PFM)
sections.content: PFM systems govern budgeting, accounting, procurement, and reporting. Transparency portals and audit institutions strengthen financial discipline and curb misuse.

sections.title: Challenges and Reform Priorities
sections.content: Capacity gaps, data fragmentation, and delayed reporting hinder efficient financial governance. Digitization, training, and harmonized standards drive reform progress.

sections.title: Historical Context of Fiscal Reforms
sections.content: Fiscal governance evolved from manual, centralized processes toward integrated information systems and multi‑tier planning frameworks supporting federal devolution.

sections.title: Expenditure Control and Risk Management
sections.content: Commitment controls, cash forecasting, and internal audit risk matrices manage liquidity, reduce arrears, and detect irregularities early.

sections.title: Procurement Modernization
sections.content: E‑procurement portals, standardized bidding documents, and supplier performance tracking enhance competition, value for money, and integrity in contracting.

sections.title: Case Study: Capital Project Oversight
sections.content: A multi‑year infrastructure project uses milestone-based disbursements and dashboard reporting, reducing delays and cost overruns through real‑time variance alerts.

sections.title: Future Outlook
sections.content: Next phase: accrual adoption pilots, open fiscal data APIs, program budgeting expansion, and analytics for predictive revenue and expenditure management.

summary: Budget lifecycle integrates planning, execution, & audit loops
Historical reforms digitized and decentralized fiscal management
Equalization & shared revenues pursue inter‑regional equity
PFM controls + risk management reinforce fiscal discipline
Case oversight dashboards curb overruns in capital projects
Reform challenges: capacity, data integration, timeliness
Future: accrual pilots, program budgeting & predictive analytics
